label: Reserves (import cover)
note: How many months of imports the reserves would cover. The buffer that decides whether a shilling shock has to be met by borrowing. CBK publishes this weekly against a statutory floor of four months; USD 14,699 million on this date, about KSh 1.91 trillion at 129.96, down from USD 14,740 million (also 5.9 months) a week earlier and below 15,088 million (6.1) on 17 September. Weekly Bulletin of 6 November 2026, read by the cbk-watch function from CBK's own PDF.

label: Gross domestic debt
note: What the government owes at home, the pool every auction on this site draws from. KSh 7,894.42 billion at 30 October 2026 (Weekly Bulletin of 6 November, gross domestic debt), up from 7,884.79 billion a week earlier. Read by the cbk-watch function from CBK's own PDF.

label: Public debt (total)
note: Everything the government owes, domestic and external together — KSh 13,475.15 billion at end-August 2026, provisional (CBK Weekly Bulletin of 23 October 2026, Table 11: domestic 7,676.02bn + external KSh 5,799.13bn, which reconcile to the total; external US$ 44.80bn), up from 13,228.89bn at end-July. Shown as a level; the ratio to GDP is the IMF's, in the Government debt / GDP row.

label: Current account / GDP
note: The gap between what Kenya earns from and pays to the rest of the world — US$ 3,785.1 million in the year to May 2026, against US$ 2,247.4 million (1.7%) a year earlier. A wider gap has to be financed by capital inflows or reserves. Read from the owner-supplied Q4 FY2025/26 QEBR, para 25.

label: External debt stock
note: US$ 43,897.2 million at June 2026, up US$ 1,428.1 million on the year: 54.6% multilateral, 27.0% commercial, 18.2% bilateral. Owed in foreign currency, so a weaker shilling raises its cost. Q4 FY2025/26 QEBR, para 15.

label: Interest / government revenue
note: Interest on all public debt, KSh 1,074.4 billion, against ordinary revenue of KSh 2,588.4 billion in FY2025/26 — computed from QEBR paras 36 and 40, which do not print the ratio. Up from about 24% on the World Bank's 2023 general-government basis; the bases differ, but the direction is the story. Interest is paid before any other spending.

label: Fiscal balance / GDP
note: The FY2025/26 outturn: a deficit of KSh 1,264.7 billion on a commitment basis including grants, against a 7.3% target and 6.7% the year before (QEBR paras 47-48). Every shilling of it is borrowed, most of it at the auctions this site covers. The IMF's 2025 estimate, on a general-government calendar-year basis, was -6.4%.

label: GDP growth
note: Whether the economy behind the borrowing is still expanding. Real GDP grew 5.1 percent in 2026Q2 against 4.9 percent in 2025Q2, led by services (5.8 percent); agriculture slowed to 3.5 and industry to 4.4. KNBS figures as reported in the CBK Weekly Bulletin of 23 October 2026, Table 1 and page 1 text. Growth is what eventually pays debt down without new borrowing.

label: Diaspora remittances, 12 months
note: The largest regular source of dollars into Kenya, and the reason the shilling has held near 130. September 2026 brought US$ 438.5 million (+4.5 percent on a year earlier, below August's record US$ 451.8 million); the twelve months to September total about US$ 5.03 billion, 1.0 percent under a year earlier. North America is weakening (-11.2 percent January to September) while Europe set a monthly record. Not read from CBK's release: five outlets agree on the monthly figure, and give the twelve-month total between 5.01 and 5.03, so treat the second decimal as approximate. Replace with the CBK document when supplied.

label: Goods trade deficit, 12 months
note: The dollars Kenya must find each year to pay for what it imports, which is what the shilling and the reserves rest on. In the twelve months to July 2026 goods exports were US$ 13.49 billion against imports of US$ 26.34 billion. Twelve months to August 2025 the gap was US$ 10.64 billion: imports have grown 12.0 percent over that span and exports 4.8 percent, and the current account deficit widened from US$ 2.81 billion to US$ 4.64 billion. Oil explains part of it: the table prints Murban crude at US$ 116 a barrel in March 2026 against US$ 71 in July 2025. Balance of payments figures are provisional until KNBS releases its quarterly data. Read from CBK's Monthly Economic Indicators for July 2026 by the cbk-watch reader.
